sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Gravitas** ​(*gravitas*) ‌— Weight, ‌Seriousness, ​Dignity ​· ​Weight, importance ​— ​belongs ‌to ​the Greek ​tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is catalogued ​under ‌the ​domain ​"Weight, Seriousness, ​Dignity". ​The ​name ‌means "Weight, ​importance".

‌**Gravitas** ​is ‌weight, seriousness, ​dignity. ‌The ​name ‌means "Weight, ​importance" ​and ‌belongs ‌to the ‌greek ​tradition.

​PuniCodex ‌restores the ​name ​as ‌**Gravitas** ​and serves ​its ‌temple ​at ‌[its temple](https://punicodex.com/gravitas/). ​The ​original ​preserves ​one prosodic ‌feature ‌— ​stress ‌or vowel ​length ​— ‌rather ‌than both, ‌which ‌places ​the ‌name in ​Tier ​2. ​The ‌plain ASCII ​form ​*gravitas* ​survives ‌as a ​modern ​convenience ​imposed ‌by the ​early ‌domain-name ​system; ‌the restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, ​is the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation survives ‌for ​this name; ​**Gravitas** is ​a ​scholarly transliteration ​of the ‌reconstructed ​spoken form. ​Etymologically the ‌name ​means "Weight, ‌importance".

The ​ASCII ‌form *gravitas* ​survives only ​because ​the early ​domain-name system ​could ‌not carry ​diacritics; it ‌is ​a technological ‌compromise, not ​an ‌ancient spelling. ​The Unicode ‌restoration ​**Gravitas** recovers ​the full ‌diacritic ‌detail of ‌the scholarly ​transliteration ​directly in ‌the address ​bar. ​The original ‌preserves one ​prosodic ​feature — ‌stress or ​vowel length ‌— ​rather than ​both, which ​places ​the name ‌in Tier ‌2.

​The letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

​- ​**g** → ‌**G** — ‌G ‌uppercase
- ‌**r** → ​**r** ‌— r ​same
- ​**a** ​→ **a** ‌— a ​same
​- **v** ​→ **v** ‌— ​v same
​- **i** ​→ ‌**i** — ​i same
‌- ​**t** → ‌**t** — ​t ‌same
- ‌**a** → ​**a** ​— a ​same
- ​**s** ‌→ **s** ‌— s ​same

sections.label: Pronunciation
sections.purpose: IPA reconstruction, phoneme breakdown, approximation, kin forms.
sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/gravitas/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**gravitas** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Gravitas.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"gravitas" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Gravitas".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"gravitas" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Gravitas" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Gravitas was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Gravitas ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Gravitas ‌place ​weight, seriousness, ​dignity ​at the ​center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

‌### Origins ​(Myth)

‌Gravitas appears ​in ‌greek ​tradition as ​weight, ​seriousness, dignity. ​The ​name's ‌meaning, "Weight, ​importance", ‌shapes ​the narratives ‌told ​about this ‌figure.

​### ‌Worship and ​Memory ​(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ​Gravitas ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name ​survived into ‌the ​modern scholarly ‌record.

​The ​myths of ​Gravitas ​survive in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, ​and later ‌retellings. ​Each ​version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ‌its ‌tellers ​— poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The ‌PuniCodex entry ​does ​not ​privilege a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the ‌attestations so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Gravitas ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.label: Archaeology & Material Evidence
sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Gravitas ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Greek ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Gravitas, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​weight ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Gravitas is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of weight, ​Seriousness, ‌Dignity ​in ​the ‌mind and ​to ‌ask ​what ‌of it ​endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"Weight, importance" ‌— ​and ‌a ​name that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​weight, ‌Seriousness, ​Dignity ​· ‌Weight, importance.

​Sit ‌with ​the ​restored ​form — ​Gravitas ‌— ‌and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ​become ​the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ‌a ​small ‌act ​of attention, ​a ​refusal ‌to ​let the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form ​*gravitas* ​stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
